checks.title: Entry-timing difference is declared
checks.detail: kernel enters at the hourly close; the live bot scans every 5 min on a forming candle, so the kernel reads pumps +0.54pp larger on average (224 matched setups). DECLARED LIMITATION: arena absolute WR is not live WR. Arm-vs-arm comparisons stay valid — all arms share this kernel — but a promoted arm must still survive the earlier live entry, and that caveat is attached to every surfaced verdict.

findings.claim: CHECKLIST arms_running: '5 running: tp-7pct, hold-12h, entry-8pct, sl-5pct, vol-4x' is green and critical.
findings.problem: The arena listing shows seven arms in state running/confirm, including control and placebo, but the check counts only five. Whatever the intended definition, the green detail string and the arena table disagree about how many arms are running, and a critical check whose count does not reconcile with the arm registry is exactly the META failure mode that hid firstred-1h for six weeks.

findings.claim: entry-8pct is reported as [running/confirm] alongside the other confirm arms.
findings.problem: It has live_n=5 against a planned confirm n=600 and declined=79 versus 47 for the shared-detection arms, so it is accumulating live evidence at roughly a fifth of the rate of control. At the measured 24.9 control trades/day ghost arrival with 79% declined, this arm cannot reach the planned sample on any timescale comparable to the others, yet its status carries the same 'confirm' label with no flag that its horizon differs by an order of magnitude.

findings.claim: paired_population is green: '4848 events in the shared window; every arm has seen all of them'.
findings.problem: The arms' own screen_n values are not consistent with a single shared population: control/placebo=1560, hold-12h=1563, sl-5pct=1560, tp-7pct=1556, vol-4x=874, entry-8pct=498. hold-12h has MORE scored screen events than control, which cannot happen if the detection stream is identical and only max_hold_h changed. The check establishes that events were offered to every arm, not that arms are scored on the same events — which is the property the paired comparison actually needs.

findings.claim: Screen deltas are quoted as decision-relevant, e.g. hold-12h screen_dWR=3.27pp and sl-5pct screen_dWR=5.26pp.
findings.problem: These are computed on the backfill tier (4764 backfill events vs 84 live), and backfill_cannot_promote confirms no arm may promote on them. But screen_dWR for the two entry_trigger arms and vol-4x is reported as 0.0pp while their screen_wr differs from control's 50.128 (entry-8pct 51.807, vol-4x 51.487) — so the dWR field is not a uniform 'delta vs control on the same window'. Reporting a level for some arms and a delta for others under one column name violates the 'never quote a level' rule.

findings.claim: Every screen statistic above is presented as evidence about the arms.
findings.problem: Not one screen_wr or screen_ev in the arena is accompanied by a dispersion or a p-value, and the corrected alpha of 0.00833 is stated but never applied to any reported comparison. sl-5pct's screen_ev of 0.042 is BELOW control's 0.051 while its screen_dWR is quoted as +5.26pp — a win-rate dial that costs expectancy, which is precisely the G-08/G-17 failure mode — yet nothing in the reported status marks that contradiction.

findings.claim: kernel_agreement is green at '219/224 live setups reproduced (97.8%)' with a 90% floor.
findings.problem: Four of the five misses are the same coin (BOME) within eight days, so the failures are not independent draws from the 224 — they are one systematic gap in one name. A pass/fail threshold on a pooled percentage cannot detect a per-coin blind spot, and BOME sits in the thin-alt population that G-40/G-41 identify as where the entire edge lives.
